# Recommended-book metadata collection

2026-10-25, Europe/Warsaw. Books were queued by their initial unrounded repository scores. Each new numeric field counts once per book toward the requested 1,000 data points. Search-link replacements are additional and reported separately. Repeated evidence, edition attributes, attempted requests and score recalculations do not count toward the target.

| Change | Count |
|---|---:|
| Page counts added | 462 |
| Reference-page counts added | 541 |
| Amazon rating aggregates added | 9 |
| Generic Amazon searches replaced with print-ISBN URLs | 270 |
| Total changes | 1282 |

1093 books improved; 563 scores recalculated to different totals. Link replacements have verified print identifiers, but **the Amazon endpoints remain untested**. They are not claimed as confirmed live product pages or stock checks. No zero-rating aggregate was established. Blocked pages and missing rating widgets remain unknown.

Library ISBN batches were paced at least 3.5 seconds apart, Internet Archive batches at least 10 seconds apart, and public Google Books previews at least 6 seconds apart. The direct Amazon request encountered an access challenge and stopped; Google Books API requests stopped on a quota limit. No proxy rotation, login, CAPTCHA bypass or regional switching was used. Older saved Amazon HTML is identified as historical evidence, not a fresh rating snapshot. The maximum among matching inspected cached aggregates is used, without adding counts. There is no claim to an exhaustive edition search.

Reference counts cover only documented bounded sections, exclude indexes, and may be incomplete where a catalog omits separate notes. Preliminary Roman-numbered pages and separately numbered plates are not added to a catalogued main-page extent. Underlying metadata usually has moderate confidence; differing or unconfirmed edition ratios have low confidence. Each record identifies its source and edition.

Eligibility, content assessments, density judgments, thematic deductions, original publication ages and source membership are retained. O15 is recalculated only for new verified rating counts. R&D is rebuilt as 20 × reference pages / total pages, with explicit zero fallback for unknown inputs. Relevance is unchanged. All totals use unrounded inputs.

Machine-readable evidence and changes: [review.json](../data/metadata1000_261025/review.json), [library](../data/metadata1000_261025/library.json), [archive](../data/metadata1000_261025/archive.json), [Google previews](../data/metadata1000_261025/google-html.json), [cached Amazon](../data/metadata1000_261025/cached-amazon.json).

## Verification and held candidates

**1012 new numeric fields**, excluding 270 link replacements. Indexed Google Books bibliographic tables supplied further length and bounded contents data; saved search responses identify each result. One Amazon aggregate (AI Snake Oil) was recovered from a public web cache; its snapshot limitation is retained. No live Amazon product endpoint was confirmed.

Single-volume or abridgment candidates for The History of the Standard Oil Company, On What Matters, Hitler: A Biography, and A Study of History were held because the catalog's whole-work scope was unclear. The Incredible Journey candidate had an ambiguous expanded title. The Inconvenient Truth candidate was a shorter adaptation. Future-dated editions were rejected. Other pre-existing series/identity holds remain in the collection scripts. No held value counts toward the target.

Skidelsky's 2003 John Maynard Keynes entry names the one-volume edition, so its matching one-volume metadata is retained. The Paine entry explicitly names Volume 2. Tombstone's English translation is condensed from the Chinese original; this is disclosed in its saved edition evidence. Large-print editions are labelled; cross-edition R&D ratios remain low-confidence estimates. For God: A Human History, a documented standard-print reference range was selected over the large-print range. The phrase young readers in A Little History of Religion describes the same edition's intended readership, not a separately adapted edition; this metadata task does not reopen its prior eligibility assessment. The word adapted in The Berlin Wall describes the wall, not a book adaptation.

Automated verification checks positive page counts, bounded reference ranges, identity matches, distinct changed fields, unchanged source membership and raw criterion judgments, and recomputed scores. Metadata confidence is generally moderate; it is not a claim that every catalog record has been checked against a physical copy.
